This Appeal, Coming On For Hearing, This Day, The
Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

This appeal is filed under Section-173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'MV Act' for brevity) by the appellant-insurance company, calling in question the judgment and award dated 07.09.2011, passed in M.V.C.No.432/2007, on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Puttur, (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal' for brevity).

Brief facts:
2. On 02.09.2006 at about 7.00 p.m., when the claimant was moving by the side of Mangalore Puttur Main road for the purpose of catching an autorickshaw as a pedestrian, and when the reached a place near Hotel Ganesh Prasad Puttur, a motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-21-J-3759 came from opposite side and dashed against the claimant.
Due to the impact, the claimant sustained grievous injuries.
3. Hence, a claim petition was filed by the appellant-claimant under Section-166 of the M.V. Act, claiming compensation for the injuries suffered in the accident.

sentences.text:
Tribunal on appreciating the materials on record, allowed the claim petition in part,
and awarded a compensation of Rs.53,000/-, along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realisation.
The Tribunal held respondent Nos.1 and 2 therein, jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

4. Heard arguments of the learned counsel for the parties and perused the materials on record.
5.

The learned counsel for the appellant - insurance company submitted that in the present case it is stated that the accident has occurred on 02.09.2006, but the complaint is lodged on 01.12.2006 before the JMFC, Mangalore and based on that, FIR is registered which produced as Exhibit-P1.
Further, there is no reason stated for such delay in lodging the complaint.

6. Furthermore, submitted that even though it is stated that the claimant had taken initial treatment at Mahaveer Hospital, Puttur and later at Colaco Hospital, Mangalore, no evidence is produced for having taken treatment in the said Mahaveer Hospital, Puttur.

Further, submitted that even though the claimant produced the medical records Colaco Hospital Mangalore, but in the said documents there is no mention about the history of the accident, when the claimant was admitted to the hospital.
7. Furthermore, there is no complaint, spot- sketch, spot-mahazar, IMV investigation report, etc., to prove the factum of accident.

But just because the charge- sheet is filed and permitting before the Court and making claim for amount is not sufficient for proving that the accident was caused involving the vehicle stated in the complaint and the claimant had suffered injuries.

Therefore,
submitted that there are no evidence to prove the factum of accident, the claimant having sustained injuries in the road traffic accident, taking treatment, and involvement of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, submitted that claim petition is fraudulent which is filed just to make claim against the insurance company.
Therefore, prays to set-aside the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.
8. On the other hand, the learned counsel for the respondent - claimant justified the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.
9. In the present case, even though the accident was stated to be caused on 22.09.2006 but FIR is registered is on 01.12.2006.

In the FIR, the reason is stated that since the owner of the offending vehicle had promised to reimburse the medical expenses, Hence, First Information Statement (FIS)
was not filed, but since the owner did not reimburse the medical expenses, therefore FIS was lodged.
This is the only explanation offered for the delay in lodging compliant .
The claimant has not produced the first information statement (FIS) given to the Police.

The submission is considered as the claimant has filed private complaint under Section-200 of Cr.P.C., before the JMFC, Mangalore,
just to obtain registration of FIR and that is produced.
But admittedly FIS lodged before the Police is not produced before the Tribunal.

sentences.text: Exhibit-P4 is charge-sheet which is also incomplete and a copy of the order in which driver of the offending vehicle having pleaded guilty and paid the fine amount, which are not sufficient evidence to prove the factum of accident.
The claimant has not produced spot- mahazar, spot-sketch and IMV inspection report and also FIS lodged before the Police.
Therefore, suspicion arises, whether really the accident was caused as narrated in the claim petition and the claimant had sustained injuries.
11. Furthermore, it is stated that after the accident immediately the claimant was admitted to Mahaveer Hospital, Puttur and he was for one day in the said hospital and got discharged on 23.09.2006.
But there is no medical evidence from the Mahaveer Hospital Puttur for having taken treatment in the said hospital.

Then on 11.11.2006, the claimant was admitted to Colaco Hospital,
Mangalore, but in the said medical records there is no history of accident and it is not stated that the claimant has suffered injuries in the road traffic accident.
12. Therefore, for the facts and circumstances discussed above doubt arises about whether really the accident has occurred and the claimant had suffered injuries in the said accident.
The judgment of the Tribunal is a cryptic in nature without appreciation of evidence on record.
There is no proper assessment of evidence much less, appreciation of the circumstances surrounding the factum of the accident alleged in the claim petition.
Therefore, awarding of compensation by coming to the conclusion and that there was a road traffic accident and the claimant had sustained injuries is baseless without any evidence.
Thus, this is a perverse approach by the Tribunal.
Therefore, the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is illegal and perverse and thus is liable to be set-aside and accordingly set-aside.
Hence, appeal filed by the insurance company deserves to be allowed.

13. Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i. The appeal is Allowed.
ii.
The impugned judgment and award dated 07.09.2011, passed in M.V.C.No.432/2007, on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Puttur is set-aside.
iii. The amount in deposit be refunded to the appellant-insurance company forthwith.
iv. Registry is directed to return the Trial Court Records to the Tribunal, along with certified copy of the order passed by this Court forthwith without any delay.
v. No order as to costs.
